html:
Bhagat Singh was an Indian revolutionary, born in 1907 in a village of the Punjab canal colonies, who was hanged by the British in Lahore in 1931 at the age of 23.

He turned to socialism and armed struggle and joined the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

In 1928 the nationalist leader Lala Lajpat Rai was beaten by police at a protest and died soon after. To avenge him, Bhagat Singh and Shivaram Rajguru shot dead a young police officer, John Saunders, in Lahore, mistaking him for the officer they meant to kill. In April 1929 he and Batukeshwar Dutt threw two harmless bombs into the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi, shouted Inquilab Zindabad, "long live revolution", and let themselves be arrested.

In prison he led a long hunger strike and wrote essays, including "Why I Am an Atheist". He was convicted for the Saunders killing and hanged on 23 March 1931 with Rajguru and Sukhdev. Gandhi, who rejected violence, was blamed by many for not saving him. He remains a hero in both India and Pakistan.
